not_modelled.what: Department of Defense Survivor Benefit Plan annuity payments share the Military Retirement Exclusion (up to 20,000 a return, federal AGI limits 125,000 / 250,000); the projection covers only military retirement pay, as it can't tell a Survivor Benefit Plan annuity from other annuities.
Blind exemption credit of 153 for each spouse who is visually impaired, reduced above the same federal AGI amounts as the other exemption credits.
Dependent exemption credit of 475 for each dependent, reduced by 6 for each 2,500 (1,250 married filing separately) of federal AGI over 252,203 / 504,411 / 378,310.
Interest on U.S. savings bonds, Treasury bills, notes and bonds and other U.S. obligations (and qualifying mutual-fund exempt-interest dividends) is subtracted (Schedule CA line 2, column B).

approximations.what: The exemption credits' AGI limitation is a stepped phase-down (each credit loses 6 for each 2,500 of federal AGI, or part of it, over 252,203 single and married filing separately, 504,411 joint and qualifying surviving spouse, 378,310 head of household; 1,250 steps when filing separately). The projection has no field for unprinted step amounts, so it removes the personal and senior credits at the threshold.
approximations.size: Only for federal AGI within 62,500 above the threshold (31,250 filing separately): up to 147 a credit just over it, falling by 6 a step to nil. A joint couple both 65 at AGI 505,000 is charged 588 (4 x 147) too much.

approximations.what: A qualifying surviving spouse gets 2 personal exemption credits (Form 540 line 7, status 5); a per-person evaluation gives one.
approximations.size: 153 a year for a qualifying surviving spouse below the AGI limit.

approximations.what: The Military Retirement Exclusion is applied every year; the booklet says it is for taxable years beginning before 2030-01-01. Scheduled changes are a pending feature (tax-reference-data issue #2).
approximations.size: From 2030: the marginal rate x up to 20,000, about 1,860 at 9.3%.

approximations.what: The Behavioral Health Services Tax (1% of taxable income over 1,000,000) is folded into the brackets for every status, so in the projection it is part of the tax that credits can reduce; on Form 540 it is added on line 62 after credits.
approximations.size: Nil for the exemption credits (they are gone well below 1,000,000 of AGI); only matters for other credits a projection does not model.

approximations.what: The standard deduction is always applied; California allows itemized deductions instead (Form 540 line 18, Schedule CA Part II), which differ from the federal ones and are limited above federal AGI of 252,203 / 504,411 / 378,310.
approximations.size: Depends on the household's California itemized deductions (mortgage interest, property tax, charity); for an itemizer usually larger than 5,706 / 11,412, so the projection then overstates tax.

approximations.what: IRA and pension distributions are taken at their federal taxable amount; California may tax a different amount when California IRA basis differs from federal (Schedule CA line 4, FTB Pub. 1005), including on a Roth conversion.
approximations.size: Nil for most households; only where IRA contributions were deducted differently for California and federal purposes.

approximations.what: Interest on U.S. Treasury and other U.S. obligations is taxed (the projection cannot tell it from other interest).
approximations.size: The marginal rate x the Treasury interest: 9.3% of 10,000 is 930 a year.

approximations.what: A projection that cannot tell California bonds from other states' bonds treats all tax-exempt interest as other-state and adds it back.
approximations.size: The marginal rate x the interest from California state and local obligations.

approximations.what: Taxable income of 100,000 or less is taxed by the Tax Table (100-dollar rows, tax at the row midpoint); the projection uses the schedules' exact arithmetic.
approximations.size: Under 5 dollars a year (half a row times at most 9.3%).

approximations.what: The senior exemption credit counts a person whose 65th birthday is on January 1 of the next year as 65; an age-at-year-end test misses that one year.
approximations.size: 153 once, for a person born on January 1.

derived_figures.what: 12.3% top bracket plus the 1% Behavioral Health Services Tax over 1,000,000 of taxable income, folded into the brackets (single and married filing separately from 1,000,000; joint from 1,485,906; head of household from 1,010,417)
11.3% bracket plus the 1% surtax, for joint (1,000,000 to 1,485,906) and head of household (1,000,000 to 1,010,417)
